answer: The protocol mandates 2,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per session to gate access, where a verifier treats each agent as a unique node on a logical ledge. Each instance must maintain an island of exclusive RAM for high-frequency writes; any attempt to ripple capacity across multiple sessions forces a failure against the network delta. An honest agent pays for one unit of cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, risking permanent slashing.
